layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Sandboxing untrusted components. When a component's code cannot be trusted, lan-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: guage-level access control is insufficient, since a malicious component with access to the host

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: runtime can reach the underlying objects directly, rendering such checks moot. Sandboxing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: requires an execution boundary beyond the reach of language-level means, such as software

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fault isolation [59], a separate language runtime, a sandboxed process, or a virtualized con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tainer [60]. Whatever the mechanism, the untrusted component runs in its own sandboxed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: context and reaches host-provided dependencies through a bridge, generalizing the cross-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: process invocation of Section 6.2: the same transparency argument renders this bridged access

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: indistinguishable from local injection. On the host side, the bridge is an ordinary fiber whose

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: capabilities can be attenuated by the access control described above.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 6.4. Language Independence and Selection

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Although Cordis is implemented in TypeScript, the context paradigm is language-agnostic:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: spatiotemporal composability is defined only by its two composability dimensions, and thus

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can be realized in any language that meets certain requirements along both. We analyze these

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: requirements along each dimension in turn.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Temporal composability. At its most basic, temporal composability requires closures: a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: revertible effect pairs an action with an inverse, and that inverse must be captured as a value,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: along with the state it restores, so it can be replayed on teardown. Beyond this, a component's

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: code and the side effects of loading it must be introducible and retractable at runtime.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: How a language meets this second requirement depends on its execution model. In

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: managed runtimes, this takes the form of a programmatic module registry, where a loaded

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: module can be evicted from the registry and garbage-collected once unreferenced; Node.js,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for instance, exposes such a registry.6 Native code exposes no module registry, so introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and retraction take the form of explicit dynamic linking and unlinking (e.g., dlopen/dlclose

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on Unix, LoadLibrary/FreeLibrary on Windows) [61], i.e., loading object code into a running

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: process and later detaching it. WebAssembly takes one path or the other depending on its

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: embedder: a module instance is reclaimed by the host's collector under a managed embedder

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (e.g., a JavaScript host), or released when a native embedder drops it (e.g., Wasmtime). Across

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: these mechanisms, the revertible effects model treats loading as an effect on the context, with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inverses that undo the registration of symbols, types, or handlers the module introduced.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Spatial composability. Spatial composability requires a mechanism for components to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: declare their dependencies and for the runtime to provide and inject these dependencies. This

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reduces to a dependency injection (DI) problem [39], which manifests at two levels that differ

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: across languages: how dependencies are typed and how their access is mediated.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: At the type level, the language should provide a way for developers to express well-typed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dependency access. A consumer obtains a coeffect by reading its key from the context, so the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: context type (Section 3.2.1) must record each key's coeffect. Typeclasses (Haskell) [62] and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: traits (Rust) [63] achieve this by letting a provider extend the context type from its own

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: module through an instance or impl [64]. TypeScript's module augmentation [65] likewise lets

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a provider module merge declarations into the context type.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: At the runtime level, dependency access must be dynamically mediated: the coeffect behind

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a key may change as providers are loaded and unloaded, and may be resolved differently across

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 6CommonJS exposes the module cache via require. cache; ES modules provide no public eviction API, though

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: modules can still be managed through engine-internal interfaces.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: contexts. The language therefore needs a way to interpose on access transparently, leaving

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the consumer's code unchanged, e.g., via JavaScript's Proxy object [66] or Python's descriptor

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: protocol

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: . Absent such a primitive, runtime reflection [68, 69] can mediate access

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dynamically, at the cost of type safety and developer experience.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Across both levels, metaprogramming facilities supply the typing and the mediation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: together. Annotations [70] and decorators attach metadata to a declaration, which a processor

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: expands into the accessor that mediates access; compile-time metaprogramming (e.g., Rust

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: procedural macros, Scala macros [71], Zig comptime) emits, for each dependency, a typed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: declaration together with such an accessor, dispensing with a general-purpose interception

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: primitive.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 6.5. Mutual Dependencies and Component Granularity

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In the reactive coeffect model, a dependency cycle simply leaves the involved components

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: permanently inactive: given two components A and B, if A requires a key provided by B and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: B a key provided by A, neither's satisfaction predicate can ever become true. Unlike deadlock

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in concurrent systems, which depends on the schedule and must be detected as it happens,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: this condition is predictable from the dependency declarations alone, so a runtime can report

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: it when components are loaded.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In practice, most apparently mutual dependencies can be decomposed into finer-grained

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: components that eliminate the cycle. Consider two components: a server (providing a network

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interface) and an access controller (enforcing authorization policies). The two components

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interact bidirectionally: the access controller mediates requests arriving at the server, and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: server exposes an endpoint for modifying access-control policies. A monolithic design would

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: make each component depend on the other. However, the two interaction directions are logi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cally independent concerns. Decomposing them yields four components: server-core, access-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: control-core, request-mediation (depending on both cores to apply access control to incoming

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: requests), and policy-management (depending on both cores to expose policy modification via

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the server). Through this approach, the cycle is eliminated because neither core depends on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the other; only the integration components depend on both.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This decomposition is always possible in principle, since every bidirectional interaction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can be factored into independent unidirectional bindings, but it increases the number of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: components: in the general case, given n mutually interacting components, the number of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: integration components can grow quadratically with n, since each pair of interacting compo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nents may require a distinct component for each direction of interaction. This does not affect

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: correctness or runtime performance (components are lightweight), and finer granularity can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be beneficial: users gain the ability to load only the specific integration bindings they need,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effectively increasing the system's composability. However, it may affect developer experience:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: more components require more configuration, more naming, and more cognitive overhead in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: understanding the dependency graph.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mitigating this granularity cost is an engineering concern rather than a theoretical one.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Practical strategies include package bundling (i.e., grouping related fine-grained components

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: into a single installable unit), convention-based wiring (i.e., automatically connecting compo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nents whose names or types match a pattern), and scaffold tooling (i.e., generating boilerplate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: integration components from declarative specifications). These strategies preserve the formal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: guarantees of the acyclic model while reducing the authoring burden to something closer to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the monolithic case.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 6.6. Dependency Typing and Versioning

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In the formal model, a dependency link is established purely by key identity: a component

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: providing key k satisfies any component declaring k in its dependency set. The type family

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ensures type-level agreement within a single compilation unit, but this guarantee breaks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: down when components are developed and built independently, which is a common scenario

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in component ecosystems. This breakage leads to two distinct problems.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Interface drift. A provider may modify the interface associated with k (adding fields,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: changing method signatures, altering behavioral contracts) between versions, while a con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sumer compiled against an earlier interface continues to declare the same key k. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dependency is satisfied at the coeffect level

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: , yet the runtime value no longer

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: conforms to the consumer's expectations, leading to type errors, method-not-found failures, or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: silent behavioral divergence [72].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Key collision. Two independently developed providers may use the same key name k to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: denote entirely unrelated interfaces. Since key identity alone establishes the link, a consumer

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: expecting one provider's interface will accept the other's value without any compatibility

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: check. Unlike interface drift, where the provider and consumer at least share a common lineage,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: key collision involves no relationship whatsoever between the expected and actual types,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: making the resulting failures unpredictable and difficult to diagnose.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Both problems point to the same gap: the coeffect model provides only nominal linking (by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: key name) but no versioned or structural linking (by interface compatibility) [73]. We discuss

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: three approaches to the gap, from most infrastructure-coupled to most language-agnostic.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Key namespacing. Extending the key space from K to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: where P identifies the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interface-defining package, eliminates key collision by construction: independently developed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interfaces with the same local name occupy distinct keys. This is the most direct solution but

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: also the most coupled: it embeds the package namespace into the formal model itself, making

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the system dependent on an external package registry for key identity.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Peer dependencies. A lighter coupling is to declare version constraints through the host-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: language package manager [74]. This is the approach Cordis currently adopts. Component

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dependencies are semantically peer dependencies: a component does not bundle its dependen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cies internally but expects the runtime context to supply them. Package managers with peer

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dependency support

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can enforce version compatibility: if the version of the package

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: providing a key falls outside a consumer's declared peer range, the incompatibility is caught

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: at install time rather than surfacing as a runtime failure. However, this approach has two

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: limitations: (1) it depends on providers faithfully adhering to semantic versioning, which is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: an unenforceable convention; (2) package managers typically resolve each dependency to a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: single version, which prevents loading components from multiple versions of the same package

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: within one application.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Structural compatibility. A fully language-agnostic approach would replace the member-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ship check

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with a compatibility predicate that verifies the provider's actual

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interface structurally subsumes the consumer's expectation. This is analogous to structural

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: subtyping [75]: a provider satisfies a consumer if the provided interface is a subtype of the re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: quired interface. The challenge lies in defining this predicate language-agnostically: structural

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: compatibility is straightforward for record types (width subtyping) but becomes complex for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: behavioral contracts (e.g., pre/postconditions [76], effect specifications [22]), and undecidable

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: once parametric polymorphism introduces bounded quantification [77].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: These three approaches address different aspects of the problem. Designing a unified

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dependency model that combines these approaches while preserving the dynamic composition

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: guarantees of the coeffect model remains an open problem.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 6.7. Co-Design with Languages and Operating Systems

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Section 6.4 identifies the minimum a host language must supply for the context paradigm. This

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: section takes up the converse question, what a language or operating system co-designed with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the paradigm can offer beyond that minimum.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Co-design with languages. A language designed around the context paradigm can improve

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on a library in two respects: the semantics it gives to contexts, and the primitives it gives to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effects and coeffects.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Such a language can make the context implicit again while preserving the context semantics

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of Section 3.3. An imperative language already runs every statement against an implicit context,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and that single context neither tracks effects nor resolves coeffects. The context paradigm

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: instead distinguishes multiple contexts, where an operation either modifies the context it

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: runs against or derives another from it (Definition 23). An in-place realization modifies the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ambient context, just as an imperative language does. A derived realization instead introduces a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: separate context, for which the language must provide a construct. Making the context implicit

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: brings both an ergonomic and a safety benefit. (1) In a library realization, every function

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: involving effects or coeffects takes the context as an ordinary argument or a receiver, as in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Section 5.1. Where the language supplies the context implicitly, functions no longer need to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: take it. (2) Every context carries its own lifecycle state and committed view (Section 4.1). A

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: library realization passes a context as an ordinary variable, so a component may reach another

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: component's context by mistake, through a closure or a global variable. An effect it installs

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: there then leaks out of its own lifecycle, and a coeffect it reads there escapes its dependency

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: specification. Making the context implicit closes both.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Such a language can also make effects and coeffects known to its compiler. (1) For effects,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: an effect iterator (Definition 17) allocates a closure at every step to hold the inverse together

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with the state it restores. With syntax for performing an effect, a compiler can emit a single

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: state machine for the whole iteration and hold those inverses in its frame. (2) For coeffects,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the coeffect specification can be admitted into the type system, with two benefits. First, a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dependency cycle is reported at compile time instead of being left to the runtime (Section 6.5).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Second, a dependency can be compared by the structure of its type rather than by key identity

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alone, as row types do [28], which is type-level support for the structural compatibility of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Section 6.6.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Co-design with operating systems. Section 1.2.3 observes a coarse-grained substitute for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dynamic composability, where the operating system supplies temporal composability at the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: granularity of a process, and the container orchestrator above it supplies spatial composability

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: at the granularity of a service. An operating system co-designed with the paradigm would

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: support fine-grained composition, by making the coeffect specification a component declares

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the whole of what it can reach, and by providing its own resources as coeffects.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Such an operating system can supply the sandbox that Section 6.3 defers to a mechanism

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: outside the language. It does so by bounding a component to the dependencies it declares,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: supplying them when the component is loaded and leaving nothing else reachable from within

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: it, as a WebAssembly module receives its imports from its embedder at instantiation [78]. It

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can also provide the coeffect isolation and interception of Section 3.2.3 as abilities of its own,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: binding a key differently for each component and mediating the accesses it supplies.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Such an operating system can also provide its own resources as coeffects. A resource lying

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: outside the boundary is made revertible where the runtime records each acquisition against

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the component that made it (Section 6.1), and every runtime keeps a record of its own. An

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: operating system that provides the resource as a coeffect keeps that record once, since it is the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: party that hands the resource out and can attribute it to the component that asked. Memory

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and file descriptors are the immediate candidates, and tracking them for the sake of recovery

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: has been done at the kernel interface [79, 80]. Furthermore, an operating system can make

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: revertible some of the operations Section 6.1 can only withhold or compensate for. A system

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that performs a write to persistent storage transactionally can roll it back |81 |, and one built on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: copy-on-write or immutable storage reaches an earlier state by moving a pointer [82, 83].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 7. Related Work

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Dynamic composability intersects several established research areas. We survey the most

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: relevant lines of work and distinguish our contribution from each of them.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 7.1. Effect and Coeffect Systems

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Section 2 reviewed effects and coeffects as the theoretical pillars underlying our work. We

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: first situate the monadic effect systems now common in industrial practice, then survey three

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: research lines that extend effects and coeffects in directions relevant to Cordis: recasting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: algebraic effects as capabilities, giving effects a reversible semantics, and unifying effects and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: coeffects under a single graded discipline.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Monadic effect systems. One family of libraries encodes effects in the type systems of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: existing general-purpose languages, representing them as monadic values that a runtime

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: executes. ZIO in Scala [84] models a computation as ZI0[R,E,A] and Effect-TS in TypeScript

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [85] as Effect<A,E,R>, a generic type whose parameters describe its result, its typed errors,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and the services its context must supply; the fp-ts library [86] encodes the same error and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: requirement channels through Reader-based monad transformers. Two traits separate these

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: systems from Cordis. First, the tracking costs a monadic embedding: a program obtains it

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: only by being written inside the effect type, whereas Cordis tracks effects as an overlay over

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ordinary host code. Second, a requirement is discharged by interpretation, an installed service

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that supplies its operations, and when that service is withdrawn what its operations performed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: remains in place; Cordis instead pairs each effect with an inverse and re-resolves requirements

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as providers come and go (Section 3.1, Section 3.2).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Algebraic effects as capabilities. Algebraic effects (Section 2.1) make effect operations visi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ble to the type system. The extension closest to our work is Brachthäuser et al.'s Effekt language,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which reinterprets effect types as capabilities [87, 88]: an effect type expresses what a compu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tation requires from its context rather than what side effects it may produce. This perspective,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: like ours, treats the context as a mediator of capabilities. Cordis and Effekt differ in two respects.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (1) In purpose, algebraic effects make effects visible to enable modular interpretation, giving one

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: operation many handler semantics, whereas Cordis makes them visible to enable tracking and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reversion, pairing every context transformation with an inverse. (2) In setting, Effekt disciplines

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effects statically at the type level, defaulting to scope-based reasoning in which capabilities are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: second-class and confined to their lexical scope, and recovering first-class use through boxing,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which lifts that restriction by tracking captured capabilities in types; Cordis instead disciplines

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effects at runtime, aiming at complete resource recovery on component removal; Section 6.7

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: takes up what a language that made the context second class in this sense would offer.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Reversible effect semantics. A parallel line gives effects a reversible semantics rather than

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: an interpretive one. Heunen et al. [89] model side effects in a reversible setting by adapting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Hughes' arrows to dagger arrows and inverse arrows, capturing effects such as serialization

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and mutable store whose operations admit inverses. This is the formal account closest to our

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: revertible effects: both pair each effect with the means to undo it rather than discharging it

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: through a handler. The two differ in where reversibility resides, and in how much of it they

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: demand. Heunen et al. work in a denotational, categorical setting where reversibility is a global

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: property, guaranteed by construction since every computation is invertible, and the inverse is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: two-sided and recovered from the categorical structure. Cordis tracks inverses at runtime and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: requires less of them: not that the whole computation be reversible, but that each atomic effect

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: admit a one-sided inverse, supplied by the caller at the point of application rather than derived,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from which the inverse of any composite follows by composition (Section 3.1).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Graded types as unified effects and coeffects. Orchard et al. [90] proposed graded modal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: types as an umbrella notion encompassing both effect reasoning (via graded monads) and co-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effect reasoning (via graded comonads), realized in the Granule language, demonstrating that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a single type system can track both what a computation does and what it needs; more recent

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: work extends coeffects to imperative Java-like languages [91, 92] and to call-by-push-value

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [93]. All of these operate at the type level: effects and coeffects are static annotations checked at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: compile time over lexically fixed scopes. Our contribution is orthogonal to this analysis: we lift

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the same two notions to runtime mechanisms, which lets Cordis handle dynamic composition.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Temporal retraction and spatial dependency are re-resolved as the set of loaded components

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: evolves, instead of being settled once over a fixed program text.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 7.2. Programming Paradigms

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The context paradigm (Section 3.3) mediates every effect and coeffect through an explicit

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: context. This section first compares it with the functional and imperative treatments of side

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effects, and then with two established paradigms, one sharing our terminology and the other

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: our treatment of crosscutting concerns.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Explicit threading and implicit mutation. Purely functional languages make effects explicit

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in types: the State monad S → (A, S) [23] threads the environment through every computa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion, securing equational reasoning at the cost of the threading itself, every function on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: call path accepting and returning the state whether or not it touches it; the monadic effect

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: systems of Section 7.1 are this pole in industrial form. Imperative languages leave effects and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dependencies implicit at the call site, so reading what a call does to the system means reading its

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: implementation transitively, and moving or removing a call may silently break distant invari-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ants. The context paradigm takes the traceability of the first treatment and the ergonomics of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the second: effects and coeffects pass through a context the component holds, so each operation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is attributable to the context it was invoked on and hence to the component, and everything else

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stays ordinary host code. The paradigm is in this sense an overlay, realizable atop a language of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: either style: it fixes each operation's denotation and leaves its realization to the host language,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in place where the host mutates and derived where it stays pure (Definition 23).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Context-oriented programming. COP [94, 95] equips a language with layers—partial

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: method and class definitions that are activated and deactivated at runtime according to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: execution context, so that behavior adapts without the base code naming its context depen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dencies [96]. COP and Cordis coincide in treating context as a first-class, runtime-mutable

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: entity and in activating and deactivating behavior dynamically, but the resemblance is nominal.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In COP, “context" denotes the ambient execution situation (e.g., location, user, mode), and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: activation changes method dispatch within a dynamically scoped extent; a layer neither tracks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the side effects it induces nor reverts them, and activation is not governed by dependency

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: satisfaction. In Cordis, the context is the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: entity mediating effects and coeffects: activation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: runs a component's revertible effects and is driven by reactive coeffect satisfaction (Section 3.2),

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and deactivation reverts them in full. COP varies what behavior runs; Cordis composes and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reverts what effects and dependencies a component installs. Their difference is one of trade-off.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: COP folds activation into the host language's method dispatch, gaining dynamically-scoped

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: layer extents at the cost of language specificity, whereas Cordis, as a language-agnostic overlay,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resolves activation reactively over a shared context. Cordis can thus express as a coeffect only

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: COP's global, value-driven fragment: context-dependent selection among implementations,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: but not dynamically-scoped activation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Aspect-oriented programming. AOP [97, 98] modularizes a crosscutting concern into an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: aspect: a pointcut that quantifies over join points selected in the base program, and advice woven

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in at each. Cordis addresses the same problem of contextual behavior that would otherwise

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: scatter across components, but its analogue of an aspect is a coeffect: a shared point of media-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion many components declare a dependence on, so that crosscutting behavior can be reshaped

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: there without editing any of them. The two paradigms then differ on two axes. (1) Declaration

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: versus obliviousness: an AOP pointcut is oblivious and quantified, matching arbitrary join points

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: whose code is unaware it is advised, whereas Cordis confines crosscutting to the coeffects each

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: component declares, so its reach is exactly that declared surface. This yields determinacy and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: traceability: an application orchestrator can inspect and govern what cross-cuts a component

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: at the configuration layer, without reading or analyzing its source, whereas an AOP concern

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is legible only through the aspects that quantify over it. (2) Lifecycle integration: a crosscutting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: change in Cordis is carried by a component's effects, reverted when the component unloads

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and propagated reactively to its dependents, so it is one move within the dynamic composition

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model; dynamic-AOP systems [99, 100] can also weave and unweave at runtime, but as a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: standalone operation, neither bound to a component's lifecycle nor triggering re-resolution

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: among the advised code.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 7.3. Temporal Composability

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Temporal composability concerns replacing or removing a component in a running program

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: while recovering the effects it installed. Prior approaches divide by how they treat a departing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: component's state and effects: carrying state forward to a successor version, recovering effects

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: through developer-authored cleanup, reversing effects automatically within a scope fixed in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: advance, or reclaiming resources from a record the runtime accumulates by interposing on an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interface.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Stateful forward migration. A broad family of systems replaces components in a running

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: program without downtime by carrying their state forward across versions. All observe the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: same timing discipline: a component may be swapped only once it reaches a safe, interaction-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: free point. Kramer and Magee established this criterion as quiescence [53], which Vandewoude

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al. later relaxed to the less disruptive tranquility [54]; our rolling-update pattern (Section 6.2)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: enforces it by draining in-flight requests before unloading a provider. Dynamic software

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: updating (DSU) then migrates state forward through hand-written transformation functions:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Hicks et al.'s general-purpose DSU for C [101], Stoyle et al.'s type-safe update points via

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: con-freeness analysis [102], and Hayden et al.'s Kitsune [103] all map old-version data to new-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: version representations, inheriting heap objects, open files, and connections in place while

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: re-initializing whatever is left unmigrated. The same discipline extends to persistent state:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Overeem et al. [104] convert a running event store's data between schema versions through

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hand-written upgrade operations while keeping the system available. Erlang/OTP [15] takes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the same stance at the process level, migrating state through code_change/3 and recovering

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from faults by restarting supervised processes rather than reverting their effects; JavaScript's

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Hot Module Replacement (e.g., webpack [48], Vite [49]) does the same at the module level,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: handing state forward through the module.hot or import.meta.hot API across a reload. Com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pared with Cordis's module replacement (Section 5.2), these approaches migrate in-memory

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: state more gracefully: Cordis reverts the old component's tracked effects and reapplies the new

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: component's from a clean slate, so a component's own in-memory state does not survive a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reload unless placed in a longer-lived dependency, and layering DSU-style forward migration

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: atop revertible effects is future work. Cordis's approach is nonetheless more general in two

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: respects: it needs no hand-written migration functions of the kind DSU and HMR require, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: it supports unloading a component entirely and recovering its resources, not merely updating

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: one in place.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Developer-authored recovery. A second family recovers a component's effects through

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cleanup or compensation logic that the developer writes by hand. Plugin lifecycle conventions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (e.g., OSGi [52], Eclipse's extension points, IntelliJ and VSCode) delegate cleanup to developer-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: written unload callbacks; the Command pattern [105] encapsulates an operation together with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: an undo method for undo/redo stacks; the saga model [51] structures a long-lived transaction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as steps each paired with a compensating action; algebraic effect handlers can attach finalizers

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that run on teardown [106]; and event sourcing [107] retracts state by appending compensating

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: events rather than executing an inverse at all. In all of them the inverse is an unenforced duty,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: decoupled from the operation, so that a forgotten one leaks resources silently (as documented

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: empirically in Section 1.2.1). React's useEffect hook [108] comes closest to pairing an effect

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with its inverse structurally, returning a cleanup the runtime invokes before each re-execution

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and on unmount. Its shortfall is composability: a hook may be called only at the top level of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a component or another hook, never inside a conditional, loop, or nested function, and its

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effect body accepts neither an async function nor an iterator. Effects thus cannot be assembled

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from other effects or interleaved with control flow, leaving nothing from which a composite

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inverse could be derived. Cordis effects carry no such restriction: they are ordinary operations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that compose freely and may run asynchronously, and require a hand-written inverse only for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: each atomic effect, from which the inverse of any composite is derived by composition, so that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: assembling existing effects requires writing no inverses at all. This structural pairing of every

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effect with its inverse makes complete recovery an invariant of the system rather than a matter

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of developer discipline.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Statically scoped reversal. A third family reverses effects automatically, by construction,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: but confines reversal to a scope fixed in advance. Software transactional memory [109, 110],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: descended from hardware transactional memory [111], records a read/write log so that a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: group of memory operations either commits or aborts, rolling memory back to its pre-trans-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: action state. Reversible computing, from Landauer and Bennett's thermodynamic analyses

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [112, 113] to reversible languages such as Janus [114], goes further and makes every step of a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: whole computation globally invertible. Reversible process calculi build backtracking into the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: semantics itself: RCCS [115] carries a memory alongside each process and admits a step to be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: taken back when the past it leads to is causally equivalent, and Phillips and Ulidowski [116]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: derive reversible operators for CCS, ACP, and CSP uniformly while preserving their forward

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: operational semantics. Their causal-consistency criterion is the concurrent counterpart of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: order Cordis's recovery follows, an accumulator applying a component's own inverses in last-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in-first-out order and the guard of Section 4.2.2 deferring a provider's withdrawal until its

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: consumers have deactivated (Theorem 70). The reach, however, is fixed by the semantics, every

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: action performed remaining undoable, whereas a Cordis component supplies an inverse for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: each atomic effect and its accumulator brings the context back to where its composition began.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Linear types [117], RAII [4], and Rust's ownership system [63] tie a resource's release to a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lexical region. Each fixes the scope and reach of reversal statically; Cordis, by contrast, fixes no

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: such scope in advance: it reverts arbitrary context operations over a component's lifecycle, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: treats lexical resource management as complementary, appropriate for local resources within a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: single component. Verification supplies the same pairing at the granularity of a data structure.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Kim and Rinard specify and verify an inverse for every state-changing operation of a collection

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of set and map implementations, together with the conditions under which two operations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: commute, reasoning on abstract state so that orders leaving equivalent rather than identical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structures count as commuting [118]. Both of the ingredients Section 3.4 requires of a coeffect

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are therefore mechanically checkable at the interfaces most keys publish, and their reason for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: preferring an inverse to a saved copy of the state is the one Section 3.1 acts on. Their inverses

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: do not compose, each being verified for one operation, whereas a Cordis accumulator carries

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the inverses of a whole lifecycle.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Interposed reclamation. A fourth family reclaims what a component acquired without

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the component itself supplying the inverses, by recording its acquisitions at an interface the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: runtime controls. Nooks [79] wraps every call crossing the boundary between the Linux kernel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and its loadable extensions, so that the kernel objects an extension touches pass through an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: object tracker whose record tells the recovery manager what to release when the extension

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fails; shadow drivers [80] tap the same calls from the other side, recording the requests and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: configuration that determine a driver's state so that a restarted instance can be restored to it.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Akeso [119] obtains the record by compiler instrumentation instead, dividing kernel execution

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: into nestable recovery domains that log their state changes and cross-thread dependencies, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rolling a faulting request back together with every domain that depends on it. Reclamation thus

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: follows from a record the runtime maintains rather than from cleanup the developer remem-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bers to write, which makes this family the closest systems-level precedent for revertible effects.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: It differs from Cordis in vocabulary and in reach. The platform fixes what can be recorded,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: whether as release code per kernel object type, one shadow per driver class, or an inverse per

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: instrumented allocator, so a component may hold only resources the platform already knows

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: how to release; a Cordis component instead introduces effects of its own and supplies an inverse

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for each atomic one (Section 3.1). Reclamation is likewise bounded by a request that commits

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or a restart of the same extension, whereas Cordis reverts over a component's whole lifetime

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and propagates removal to its dependents, which release their own effects in turn (Section 3.2).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 7.4. Spatial Composability

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Spatial composability concerns how a component's dependencies on others are declared and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bound. Prior mechanisms divide by how binding responds to change: wiring dependencies

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: once at initialization, reacting to the availability of whole components, or propagating change

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: at the granularity of individual values.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Initialization-time dependency wiring. Two established mechanisms wire components to-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gether at initialization time. Dependency injection frameworks [39] (e.g., Spring [120], Guice,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Angular, Inversify) inject dependencies into components at initialization, and UI framework

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: context (e.g., Vue.js's provide/inject and React's Context API) passes them along a component

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tree. Some support dynamic scoping (e.g., Spring's prototype/request scopes, Angular's hier-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: archical injectors), but neither re-resolves reactively: when a provider is replaced or removed at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: runtime, existing dependents are neither deactivated nor re-initialized, and none offers lifecycle

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: management of the kind our component state machine provides. Cordis's reactive coeffects

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Section 3.2) supply this: the notification mechanism triggers lifecycle transitions whenever the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: satisfaction predicate changes.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Availability-reactive component models. The closest precedent to our reactive coeffects

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reacts to service availability. OSGi's Declarative Services and iPOJO [121, 122] let components

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: declare provided and required services, with the runtime automatically activating and deacti-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vating them as services appear and disappear; iPOJO's Gravity project [122] explicitly targets

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: autonomous runtime adaptation to changing service availability, and its provide/require

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model directly prefigures Cordis's ctx. provide/ctx. get pattern. R-OSGi [55] extends the same

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: abstraction transparently to distributed settings via RPC, mapping network failures to service-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: withdrawal events, a pattern Section 6.2 discusses as an extension of the Cordis model. All

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: these systems recover through a deactivation callback, which is limited in two ways. First, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: callback is hand-written, so resource safety rests on developer discipline and a forgotten one

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: leaks silently. Second, the callback is synchronous: should teardown require an asynchronous

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: exchange with the departing dependency, the frameworks offer no protocol to await it, forcing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a blocking wait against a reference that may already be stale. Cordis's reactive coeffects close

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: both gaps: deactivation reverts the dependents' accumulated effects, and its inertial Unloading

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: state (Section 4.4) runs asynchronous teardown to completion before acting on further change.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Value-level reactivity. Functional reactive programming (FRP) [123] and its modern incar-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nations (e.g., signals [124, 125] in SolidJS, Vue's reactivity system, Angular Signals) propagate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: change at a value-level granularity: when a signal changes, derived computations are re-evalu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ated synchronously or under a scheduler [126]. Cordis's reactive coeffects act at a component-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: level granularity, adding asynchronous lifecycle semantics that value-level propagation does

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: not model. The same granularity difference runs the other way for consistency: propagating in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a turn, in an order the dependency graph fixes, lets FRP require that no derived computation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: read a mixture of updated and stale inputs, which is glitch freedom [127], whereas Cordis has

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: no counterpart of a turn, orchestration actions arriving one at a time, and guarantees only

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that no single transition straddles two resolutions of its coeffects (Theorem 71). The two are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: complementary rather than competing: a Cordis coeffect can itself carry reactive values, and a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: component updates on only the parts it actually consumes, refining component-level reactivity

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: into finer-grained reactive coeffects that span both levels.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 8. Conclusion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We have presented a formal foundation for dynamic composability by lifting the classical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: concepts of effects and coeffects to runtime mechanisms. Revertible effects address local temporal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: composability: every context transformation carries an inverse that the runtime holds, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: both tracking and recovery preserve composition, so the context is recovered upon component

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: removal. Reactive coeffects address local spatial composability: every context change is classified

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: against a component's coeffect specification as activating, deactivating, or neutral, and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: classification drives its activation and deactivation. We then unify the effect context and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: coeffect context into a single context type and mediate every effect and coeffect through it,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: yielding a discipline we call the context paradigm; the mediation induces an observational

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: equivalence up to which the effects of distinct components attain independence. Combining

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: these mechanisms into the notion of a component, we give a calculus of dynamic composition

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: whose metatheory carries spatiotemporal composability from a single component to a whole

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: system of interleaved components. We realize this paradigm as the Cordis meta-framework,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with a core library providing effect tracking and coeffect resolution, as well as a declarative

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: component loader with configuration reconciliation and hot module replacement. The Koishi

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: case study validates the design of Cordis in a production system with over 4000 community

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plugins.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Beyond human-curated plugin ecosystems, a compelling direction for future validation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is self-evolving agent harnesses (Section 1.2.2), where an AI agent generates and replaces

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: its own harness components continuously and with little human oversight. Applying Cordis

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in such a setting would validate the temporal guarantees of complete recovery under rapid

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: component replacement, as well as the spatial guarantees of dependency coordination under

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: frequent topological change. Such validation would demonstrate the paradigm's applicability

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as a foundation for recoverable, coordinated, and continuous self-evolution in agent harnesses

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and other autonomous systems.
